svg.text: ORCA crosses the geological risk sectors that CPRM/SGB publishes for all 27
states with the rain that fell on each one. Rain is hourly Open-Meteo per
sector, summed over 24h and 72h, with a forecast of where alerts are heading
in the next 72h, and one national query grid, sized by binary search, keeps
the whole country inside the free daily request budget. The dashboard is
static HTML and JS on GitHub Pages, rebuilt every day and installable as an
app: risk grade drawn as hatching like a geological map, a ruler with every
sector against a threshold you drag, live INMET warnings, radar and lightning
layers, CSV and PDF export, and your own area (GeoJSON, KML or shapefile)
processed without leaving the browser. A tutorial tab lists the thresholds
real civil defense agencies use. Sectors refresh monthly and rain daily, in
separate workflows with guards that fail the run instead of publishing a half
empty map, and 144 tests run in CI. Rain is modeled, not gauged, and the 100mm
default comes from the literature, not an official calibration. A side project
on public data, not a warning system anyone should rely on.
